title: Telangana SIR: How 73 Lakh Voters Were Marked for Deletion
shows: Frontline follows how electors in Hyderabad came to be left off Telangana's draft roll, from public data and interviews with electors, the Chief Electoral Officer, registration officers, booth level officers and party agents. It gives the 73,39,235 names left off a roll of about 3.38 crore by reason, 9,22,229 dead, 11,25,546 untraceable or absent, 45,18,963 permanently shifted, 6,70,203 already enrolled and 1,02,294 others. It reports that the SIR guidelines let a booth level officer note a probable cause for an elector whose form did not come back, and that some officers marked electors as having refused the form whether or not they had refused it. In Chandrayangutta the tentative list of names to be left off grew from 37,241 on 29 July to 1,48,869 on 11 August, and the registration officer told the magazine that names were marked on the last day. In Bahadurpura such names rose from 40,038 on 3 August to 1,21,350 at the draft. Matching the Form 9 reports of Form 6 applications that the Chief Electoral Officer published for 13 of Hyderabad's 15 seats against the names left off, by name and relation's name, it counts 2,561 electors left off who applied on Form 6, and calls the figure indicative. It also gives the Chief Electoral Officer's figures of 4,88,417 Form 6 applications in the state from 15 June to 7 October, of which about 51,821 had been added by 8 October.
quote: Telangana had around 3.38 crore electors at the beginning of the SIR, of whom more than 73 lakh were marked ASDD: 9,22,229 as dead, 11,25,546 as untraceable/absent, 45,18,963 as permanently shifted, 6,70,203 as already enrolled, and 1,02,294 under others.
On July 29, the tentative ASDD list had 37,241 electors. By August 11, it had 1,48,869, the same number as in the final ASDD list made public.
The analysis found 2,561 ASDD electors in the Form 9 records.

title: Who is being left out of voter rolls? What Aadhaar reveals about SIR
shows: Praveen Chakravarty, a Congress Member of Parliament and chairperson of the party's data analytics department, sets the count of adults with Aadhaar from UIDAI's saturation report against the rolls after the revision in 14 states. By his count 9 crore adults with Aadhaar in the 14 states are not on the rolls. In Uttar Pradesh he gives 16.3 crore adults with Aadhaar against 13.4 crore electors on the final roll, and puts the gap at 2.5 to 3 crore after allowing for deaths, people abroad and foreign citizens. He gives the gap as 21 per cent of adults in Goa, 19 per cent in Punjab and Uttarakhand and 7 per cent in Odisha and Tamil Nadu. He argues that migration cannot explain it, because no state that receives migrants has more electors than adults with Aadhaar and Bihar has one of the smallest gaps, and he replies to Surjit Bhalla's argument that the gap is adults who did not register. The column does not print the figures for each state.
quote: Across these 14 states, 9 crore adults are on Aadhaar’s servers but missing from the ECI’s rolls.
The share of missing voters ranges from 21 per cent in Goa and 19 per cent in Punjab and Uttarakhand to 7 per cent in Odisha and Tamil Nadu.
